(i) parenchymal NG2 glia and astrocytes can generate neuronal progenies in the brain, and that (ii) this neurogenic capacity is regulated by the same mechanisms that control the neurogenic potential of the SVZ.

identifying the molecular mechanisms and cellular processes that regulate neurogenesis from parenchal glia and how these processes are modulated by injury and/or reprogramming.

parenchymal neurogenesis is not a rare exception but rather a general feature of the adult brain.

parenchymal neurogenesis is a dormant program in glia that can be reawakened in the adult brain.
the neurogenic potential of glia is not restricted to specific brain areas, but is rather a property of glial cells that is regulated by local environmental cues.

parenchymal brain glia are endowed with the capacity to generate neuronal progeny and that this potential can be activated in the adult brain.
